newsitem.title: USA: Abbott results firmer in third quarter.
newsitem.headline: Abbott results firmer in third quarter.

text.p: Abbott Laboratories Inc. Tuesday reported sharply higher third-quarter results, boosted by drug sales and the pharmaceutical giant's entrance into the glucose monitoring and diagnostic imaging markets.

Profits rose 10.2 percent to $420.9 million, or 54 cents a share, in the quarter ended Sept. 30, from $382.1 million, or 48 cents a share, in the year-ago period. Worldwide sales grew 10.7 percent to $2.6 billion from $2.4 billion.
Total sales were reduced 2.6 percent due to the effect of the relatively stronger dollar, Abbott said.

"Our results reflect the effectiveness of our strategy to grow through internal product development and market expansion, complemented by external alliances and acquisitions," said Duane L. Burnham, chairman and chief executive officer.
During the third quarter, Abbott began marketing two contrast imaging agents used in radiology and cardiac catheterization procedures, in a market estimated at over $1.5 billion in the United States.

The company also expanded its alliance with SONUS Pharmaceuticals, Inc., broadening the licensing of SONUS' proprietary ultrasound contrast agent to include Europe, Latin America, Canada, the Middle East, Africa and certain Asia/Pacific Rim countries.
During the third quarter, Abbott's investment in research and development rose 9 percent to $279 million from the same period in 1995.

Abbott, which markets its products in more than 130 countries, said worldwide sales of pharmaceutical and nutritional products rose 11.7 percent to $1.456 billion in the third quarter from $1.303 billion in year-ago period. The United States accounted for $957 million of the total, while foreign sales were $499 million.
Worldwide sales of hospital and laboratory products grew 9.4 percent to $1.190 billion, with $648 million in the United States and $542 million overseas.

The Abbott Park, Ill.-based company said total sales in U.S. markets were $1.605 billion, up 13.4 percent from $1.415 billion recorded a year ago. Total international sales, including direct exports from the United States, grew 6.7 percent to $1.041 billion from $976 million a year ago.
Abbott's stock was unchanged at $50.375 on the New York Stock Exchange shortly before midday.
